analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: one added doctor bullet at head line 1025 (patch hunk @@ -1022,6 +1022,7 @@). It says App Attest serving authorization can remain visible through its unexpired lease, while MDM-removal advice needs a matching fresh coordinator decision. No source code, wire protocol, key custody, cache or fan-helper behavior changes. I examined the three supplied units, which are base text from lines 1721-2047 and head text from lines 1-396. The added line falls outside the supplied head excerpt, so I could not read it in context; I evaluated it from the patch alone. The bullet is consistent with the threat model's T-057 (premature MDM removal strands a provider), T-053 (stale authorization surviving revocation or connection change), and TB-011/A-016 (expiring authorization bound to the connection and generations). It is guidance that discourages removing MDM before a fresh decision, and it does not weaken any control. The cited ../reference/provider-authorization.md was not supplied, so the doc's accuracy against the platform-owned EvaluateAuthorization behavior is unverified; that is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression. Other unit content appears unchanged and documents existing behavior: the report upload with redaction, the environment passthrough allowlist including DARKBLOOM_APP_ATTEST_WORKER_QUALIFICATION=1, the SSD prefix-cache defaults relevant to T-041, and the add-on runtime paths for TB-012. I found no new attack surface and no invalidated threat-model assumption. The threat model does not need an update from this change.
